text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.6% today, bouncing back after a brutal two-week slide of over 10%. The stock recovered some ground as oil prices stabilized — US crude held steady around $100 per barrel and refineries ran at 94.5% capacity, supporting margins for the company's refining operations. The modest gain follows several days of sharp losses tied to geopolitical de-escalation: earlier this week, crude prices fell when President Trump suggested the Iran conflict might end soon, and market worries about new Middle East strikes eased.

The two-week decline reflects a real tension in what's good for refiners: lower oil prices on geopolitical relief sound positive in theory, but they compress the profit margins refiners earn by processing crude into fuel — the difference between what they pay for oil and what they sell gasoline for. After markets priced in much of that margin compression earlier in the week, today's modest rebound suggests traders may be anchoring on the fact that refineries are still running near capacity and fuel storage levels remain manageable, which supports near-term demand expectations.
